scenes.narration: A generator is a function that uses yield instead of return. Calling it does not run the body. It gives back a generator object. Each time you ask for the next value, the function runs to the next yield. It hands the value out, and pauses. The next request resumes right after the yield. Nothing is stored in a big list, so a generator can even be endless. Think of a conveyor belt that makes the next cookie only when you reach for it.

scenes.narration: [HL 1] A function with yield. [HL 2] This print only runs when we first ask. [HL 3] Loop while n is above zero. [HL 4] Yield hands out n, and pauses here. [HL 5] When resumed, count down. [HL 6] After the loop, print done. [HL 8] Calling countdown runs nothing yet. We only get a generator object. [HL 9] Made it. Nothing has started. [HL 10] The first next runs the body. Start. Then yield three. [HL 11] The second next resumes after the yield. Two. [HL 12] A for loop takes the rest. [HL 13] One. Then done, and the loop ends.

code.source:
def countdown(n):
    print("start")
    while n > 0:
        yield n
        n -= 1
    print("done")

g = countdown(3)
print("made it")
print(next(g))
print(next(g))
for x in g:
    print(x)

scenes.onScreen: A function box with a bookmark at the yield line; each next moves the bookmark forward
scenes.animation: A function box with a bookmark at the yield line; each next call hops the bookmark one step and ejects a value ticket
scenes.narration: Here is the picture. A generator keeps a bookmark at the yield line. Each next call resumes from the bookmark. It runs to the next yield, hands out a value, and places the bookmark again. All local variables stay alive between calls. When the function ends, the bookmark is gone, and the generator raises StopIteration.

shorts.title: What is yield
shorts.hook: "Yield works like return, but the function pauses instead of ending."
shorts.script: Yield works like return, but the function pauses instead of ending. It hands out one value, and waits. The next request resumes right after the yield. A function with yield is called a generator. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Yield pauses the function.

shorts.title: Lazy values
shorts.hook: "A generator makes values only when you ask."
shorts.script: A generator makes values only when you ask. A list of a million numbers fills memory. A generator of a million numbers holds just one at a time. It is a conveyor belt that makes the next cookie on demand. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Generators are lazy.

shorts.title: Endless generator
shorts.script: A generator can even be endless. A while True loop with a yield gives you one, two, three, forever. It never fills memory, because nothing is stored. You just stop asking when you have enough. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Endless, yet tiny.

shorts.title: Used up
shorts.script: A classic bug. You make a list from the same generator twice. The first list is full. The second is empty, and no error appears. A generator runs once. To go again, call the generator function again. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Generators run once.
